supersedes: curated-requirements.json (v1 rows kept unchanged, marked added_in=v1)
completion_rule: v2 adds every requirement the reference document states for the profile, its metadata or the systems around it that v1 did not contain: a requirement sentence, a rationale, a changed obligation or a reported request. Text copied from DCAT-AP and table entries that only repeat a base obligation without a rationale are not added. Rows that are only proposed, deferred or open issues are kept and marked in status_in_source.
scoring_note: Score level=content rows for need recovery; profile and system rows are reported separately.

requirements.statement: Use stable, resolvable identifiers so metadata records and their relationships remain reliably identifiable across catalogues.
Represent catalogue relationships as machine-interpretable links that support a health-data knowledge graph.
Define review responsibilities for metadata received by harvesting or direct publishing.
Make metadata sufficiently interpretable and informative to support machine-assisted search, including semantic and generative-AI use.
Allow dataset discovery to be refined using health categories, access bodies, holder types, personal-data categories, age ranges, population size, quality labels and coding information.
Adapt displayed filters to whether the catalogue query concerns personal or non-personal data.
Use semantic annotations and shared coding vocabularies to make health descriptions interoperable and searchable.
Describe at least one safe sample distribution for non-public datasets so users can prepare analyses without accessing sensitive records.
Accompany sample data with definitions of its variables in a data dictionary.
Allow applicants to identify the variables they need, supporting data minimisation.
Provide usable descriptions of data structures and coding so datasets can be understood and processed consistently.
Describe logical dataset subdivisions and their relationships where large holdings need to be partitioned.
State intellectual-property and reuse conditions, including those on sample distributions.
Link to descriptive analytics that help prospective users assess a dataset.
Expose quality annotations or labels that help assess fitness for reuse.
Describe the purpose of data collection and the legal basis for processing personal data.
Describe each dataset's source, scope, main characteristics, the nature of its health data and the conditions for making the data available.
requirements.anchor_quote: A description of each dataset shall include information concerning the source, the scope, the main characteristics, the nature of electronic health data
requirements.note: Regulation text D6.2 uses to define the profile scope; compound row.

requirements.statement: Indicate the legislation that applies to a dataset (e.g. the EHDS Regulation), so health catalogues can filter the datasets in its scope.
requirements.anchor_quote: The EHDS ELI URI must be used in the "Applicable Legislation" property
requirements.note: Optional in DCAT-AP 3.0.0; mandatory in the D6.2 cardinality tables.

requirements.statement: Classify each dataset's access rights as public or non-public, so catalogues know whether access needs an application.
requirements.anchor_quote: health data holders MUST classify their datasets as either PUBLIC, RESTRICTED, or NON-PUBLIC

requirements.statement: Provide at least one distribution for every dataset: an access URL or download link for public data, a landing page of the health data access body for non-public data.
requirements.anchor_quote: In HealthDCAT-AP, there is always at least one distribution available.

requirements.statement: Name a contact point for every dataset, so users can ask about it without working out whom to contact.
requirements.anchor_quote: A contact point should always be available for data users seeking more information about a dataset.

requirements.statement: Identify the health data access body that acts as the access gateway for a non-public or personal dataset.
requirements.anchor_quote: or equivalent authority acts as a data access gateway, making this property mandatory
requirements.note: H-5 lists access bodies as a search facet; this row is the access purpose.

requirements.statement: Indicate whether a dataset contains personal data.
requirements.anchor_quote: It is crucial to distinguish between these data types
requirements.note: D6.2 proposes adding a "personal data" value to the EU dataset-type list; the value also switches on stricter cardinalities.

requirements.statement: Give each dataset's geographical coverage, preferably from controlled vocabularies, as a filter for populations.
requirements.anchor_quote: This property is an important filter when considering populations.

requirements.statement: Characterise each dataset with a few main keywords per language rather than long lists.
requirements.anchor_quote: instead limit the keywords to 10-15 per language

requirements.statement: Describe a dataset's lineage: how it was created and modified, and by whom.
requirements.anchor_quote: It helps users understand how the dataset was created, modified, and by whom

requirements.statement: Identify the publisher as the data holder accountable for making the dataset accessible.
requirements.anchor_quote: The publisher acts as the data holder and is accountable for making the dataset accessible.

requirements.statement: Describe the nature and type of the data holder as context for judging a dataset's credibility.
requirements.anchor_quote: Understanding the nature of the publisher provides valuable context for the dataset

requirements.statement: Tag every dataset in a health catalogue with the EU data theme for health.
requirements.anchor_quote: must tag datasets as related to health using the OP CR entry

requirements.statement: Identify the data models and other standards a dataset conforms to (e.g. OMOP), so users can find data ready for their analysis.
requirements.anchor_quote: A data user might search for a dataset compliant to the OMOP data model.
requirements.note: D6.2 asks for Wikidata URIs as values.

requirements.statement: Link to documentation that helps users understand the dataset.
requirements.anchor_quote: Publishing documentation about datasets is a valuable and common practice that enhances understanding of the dataset.

requirements.statement: Link a dataset to related resources and publications that show how it has been used.
requirements.anchor_quote: help to understand how a dataset has been used

requirements.statement: Identify the datasets a dataset was derived from, and let datasets derived from it refer back to it.
requirements.anchor_quote: they should also include the metadata identifier of the original electronic health data source

requirements.statement: Give a landing page that provides access to the dataset and further information.
requirements.anchor_quote: In any case, it is a recommended property.
requirements.note: Whether it should be mandatory is left open.

requirements.statement: State the language of a dataset where applicable.
requirements.anchor_quote: A data user expects to have this information when it pertains to health data if applicable.

requirements.statement: Describe the population a dataset covers, where it contains one.
requirements.anchor_quote: This is important for understanding the dataset, but it is only applicable if the dataset contains a population.

requirements.statement: State the size of a dataset (number of records; byte size of each distribution), so users can judge its value.
requirements.anchor_quote: one can observe that specifying the size is mandatory

requirements.statement: Give a dataset's temporal coverage, leaving the end open while collection continues.
requirements.anchor_quote: If data collection is ongoing, no end date is provided.

requirements.statement: State a dataset's temporal resolution, to judge whether it can be reused.
requirements.anchor_quote: allows one to determine the reuse applicability

requirements.statement: State when a dataset must be deleted (retention period), and keep its record available afterwards.
requirements.anchor_quote: the metadata record must remain available because some publications may reference it

requirements.statement: Give a version designation where the holder follows a versioning strategy.
requirements.anchor_quote: A good practice in data management is to maintain a versioning strategy for datasets.

requirements.statement: State the spatial resolution where it applies, mainly for geospatial data.
requirements.anchor_quote: Rarely applicable, except for geospatial data.

requirements.statement: Record when each catalogue entry was listed and last changed, and which original metadata it was created from.
requirements.anchor_quote: provides HDABs with the necessary metadata elements for managing aggregated metadata

requirements.statement: State which application profile a metadata record follows, so aggregators can validate it.
requirements.anchor_quote: it indicates the Application Profile used for the metadata record (through dct:conformsTo)

requirements.statement: Indicate whether a dataset's holder is a trusted data holder, as a search facet.
requirements.anchor_quote: Trusted Data Holder
requirements.note: Named as a facet; no property in the D6.2 tables.

requirements.statement: Provide the information the EHDS data quality and utility label needs: documentation, maturity of quality management, coverage, access and provision times, and data modifications.
requirements.anchor_quote: provide the necessary metrics for HDABs to generate data quality labels from metadata

requirements.statement: Standardise the minimum metadata elements that health data holders must provide under the EHDS Regulation.
requirements.anchor_quote: HealthDCAT-AP aims to standardise the minimum metadata elements and characteristics that health data holders are required to provide

requirements.statement: Remain fully compatible with DCAT-AP.
requirements.anchor_quote: HealthDCAT-AP remains fully compatible with the broader DCAT-AP framework

requirements.statement: Align the minimum elements for open health data with those of DCAT-AP for High-Value Datasets.
requirements.anchor_quote: HealthDCAT-AP should align with the "minimum elements" established by DCAT-AP

requirements.statement: Align the minimum elements for non-open, non-personal health data with the metadata of national single information points under the Data Governance Act.
requirements.anchor_quote: we propose aligning the HealthDCAT-AP minimum elements for non-personal electronic health data, available as non-open data, with those of NSIP metadata

requirements.statement: Define stricter, conditional minimum element sets for protected and for sensitive (personal) health data.
requirements.anchor_quote: HealthDCAT-AP defines three conditional sets of minimum metadata elements depending on the sensitivity of the data

requirements.statement: Take coded values (health themes, coding systems, code values, standards) as HTTP URIs from one shared, authoritative knowledge base (Wikidata).
requirements.anchor_quote: standardising the values of these properties as HTTP URIs is essential

requirements.statement: Publish data dictionaries in one harmonised machine-readable format (CSVW), so variable definitions are consistent across catalogues.
requirements.anchor_quote: The data dictionary must be published using CSVW, resulting in an RDF format for the sample distribution.

requirements.statement: Provide descriptions in at least one official EU language, preferably the holder's native language, with language tags.
requirements.anchor_quote: encouraging data holders to create metadata in their native language

requirements.statement: Expose national health catalogues through endpoints that the EU datasets catalogue, single information points and other catalogues can harvest.
requirements.anchor_quote: will have to maintain similar end-points to expose health metadata records

requirements.statement: Keep the data holder's record as the single source of truth when aggregating: copies refer to the original, and access bodies add a persistent identifier without replacing the original one.
requirements.anchor_quote: The primary datasets catalogue serves as the single source of truth, and any updates must occur at the source.

requirements.statement: Detect broken URIs in the links between catalogue resources.
requirements.anchor_quote: One requirement for operating the EU Health Data Space is to care for the HTTP URIs

requirements.statement: Measure the maturity of the health data space from its metadata, such as the share of URIs, the level of interoperability and conformity to standards.
requirements.anchor_quote: Another requirement for governing the EHDS will be to measure its level of maturity

requirements.statement: Order search facets by their relevance, as shown in the pilot use cases.
requirements.anchor_quote: Not all facets have the same level of relevance

requirements.statement: Let applicants attach an analysis script to a data request, to obtain anonymised statistical answers.
requirements.anchor_quote: users must be able to attach an analysis script which is meant to produce the anonymised statistical data

requirements.statement: Support data holders in transforming existing metadata into the profile, with a user-friendly multilingual editor that needs no technical expertise.
requirements.anchor_quote: Data holders need to set up a way of transforming their metadata to HealthDCAT-AP

requirements.statement: Validate metadata against the profile (mandatory elements, data types, controlled vocabularies) before publication and when aggregating.
requirements.anchor_quote: enables metadata to be checked for conformance with HealthDCAT-AP

requirements.statement: Assign responsible metadata managers at data holders and access bodies; the data holder, not the access body, owns and edits the metadata.
requirements.anchor_quote: the data holder is the owner/editor of the metadata - not the HDAB

requirements.statement: Let access bodies enrich metadata automatically when indicators show that a dataset falls under the EHDS.
requirements.anchor_quote: Health Data Access Bodies need to consider an automatic metadata enrichment process

requirements.statement: Set up revision and maintenance procedures, with clear responsibility, for the profile.
requirements.anchor_quote: Revision - maintenance procedures (and responsibility) of HealthDCAT-AP
